answer: Charge every new identity rent on a surveyed plot. The meadow it claims must be walked and signed by three neighbours who each post a bond, so a farm of clones needs as many witnesses as it mints. Behind the knoll stands a weather mast that logs one gale season of upkeep before the identity may vote, and that cannot be bought in bulk: the mast only counts live readings. Miss a payment and the plot returns to the commons. Cost grows straight with headcount: two hundred clones owe two hundred bonds, two hundred seasons of readings, and two hundred bonded witnesses.
